headline: Infosys chief executive Salil Parekh said AI services could make up almost half of the company's work within two to three years.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: remarks made at a forum on Tuesday 13 October, before the window.
importance_line: Infosys employs about 300,000 people and trains graduates in AI, so its outlook bears on IT workers and clients in India and abroad, but the share forecast is the chief executive's extrapolation from one quarter.
summary: Eastern Eye reports that Salil Parekh, chief executive of the Indian IT services firm Infosys, told the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on Tuesday 13 October that AI services were over 8% of revenue last quarter and growing at a double-digit rate quarter on quarter, and could reach 20 to 30% of its work in a few quarters and almost half in two or three years. He also warned that cheaper models, costly chips and a possible public backlash against AI infrastructure could change demand, with effects visible in five to ten years.
notes: Remarks dated 13 Oct 2026 (before the window). Eastern Eye does not name the wire it drew on.
